Of whom the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 5:12|what have I|Quid mihi]], he says, [[1 Cor 5:12|to do to judge them that are without?|de his qui foris sunt, judicare]] This the Saviour fulfilled in some measure in person at his first coming, by preaching the gospel in Decapolis and to the men of Tyre and Sidon[[Mark 7:31||]][[Matt 15:21||]], as is plain from the Gospel. Moreover, from the beginning he made known the way of salvation to many nations through certain Patriarchs and Prophets. And after his resurrection he opened the law of the gospel to the whole world through the Apostles and the other disciples, whom he commanded: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and again, [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me|Eritis mihi testes]] [[Acts 1:8|in all Judea|in omni Judæa]] and Galilee, [[Acts 1:8|and even to the uttermost part of the earth|et usque ad ultimum terræ]] [Denis has "Galilee" where the Vulgate has "Samaria"]. He preached abroad also in the sense of openly among the people, as he testifies: [[John 18:20|I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, whither all the Jews resort: and in secret I have spoken nothing|Ego palam locutus sum mundo ; ego semper docui in synagoga et in templo, quo omnes Judæi conveniunt, et in occulto locutus sum nihil]]. Hence it is added: [[1:20|she uttereth her voice in the streets|In plateis dat vocem suam]]: because he preached through his ministers in the broad places of the roads and of the nations, to whom he gave the charge: [[Matt 10:27|that which you hear in the ear, preach ye upon the housetops|Quæ auditis in aure, prædicate super tecta]]. For, as he declared, [[John 3:21|he that doth truth cometh to the light|Qui facit veritatem, venit ad lucem]]. Nor is this contradicted by what was foretold of Christ, [[Is 42:2|He shall not cry|Non clamabit]], [[Is 42:2|neither shall his voice be heard abroad|nec audietur foris vox ejus]]: for by this only an unreasonable and unseemly clamour is denied of him. Hence the Apostle commands: [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour|Omnis amaritudo, et indignatio, et ira, et clamor]] [[Eph 4:31|be put away from you|tollatur a vobis]].

paras.t: In capite, id est in superiori parte, seu loco, vel principe, turbarum clamitat. Prædicatores namque stare solent in loco primo ac eminenti ; sed et principibus populorum sermocinari dignatus est Dominus. In foribus portarum urbis profert verba sua, dicens. Urbs ista, est Ecclesia. De qua in Psalmo : Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei ; et in Apocalypsi, Vidi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem a Deo paratam, sicut sponsam ornatam viro suo. Fores portarum urbis istius, sunt virtutes, quibus intratur in regnum ipsius, vel fides atque Baptismus, vel pastores ac prælati, qui alios in Ecclesiam ducunt. In his foribus profert Sapientia verba sua : quibus et dixit, Non vos estis qui loquimini, sed Spiritus Patris vestri, qui loquitur in vobis. Unde et unus talium scripsit : An experimentum quæritis ejus, qui in me loquitur Christus? Ad litteram quoque sapientes et judices consueverunt antiquitus residere in urbium portis, ad consulendum ac judicandum de causis sibi propositis, quatenus omnibus pateret ad ipsos accessus, et celeriter expedirentur qui accessissent. Unde in Deuteronomio jussum est : Judices constitues in portis urbium tuarum. Et sanctus Job : Procedebam, inquit, ad portam civitatis, et in platea parabant cathedram mihi.
paras.en: [[1:21|At the head|In capite]], that is, in the upper part or place, or in the prince, [[1:21|of multitudes she crieth out|turbarum clamitat]]. For preachers are wont to stand in the first and highest place; and the Lord also deigned to speak with the princes of the peoples. [[1:21|in the entrance of the gates of the city she uttereth her words, saying|In foribus portarum urbis profert verba sua, dicens]]. This city is the Church, of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 86:3|Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God|Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei]]; and in the Apocalypse: I [[Apoc 21:2|saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem|Vidi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem]] [[Apoc 21:2|from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband|a Deo paratam, sicut sponsam ornatam viro suo]]. The entrances of the gates of this city are the virtues by which one enters into its kingdom; or faith and Baptism; or the pastors and prelates who lead others into the Church. In these entrances Wisdom utters her words; to whom he also said: [[Matt 10:20|it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you|Non vos estis qui loquimini, sed Spiritus Patris vestri, qui loquitur in vobis]]. Hence one of these also wrote: [[2 Cor 13:3|Do you seek a proof of Christ that speaketh in me|An experimentum quæritis ejus, qui in me loquitur Christus?]]? In the letter, too, the wise men and the judges were wont of old to sit in the gates of cities, to give counsel and to judge the cases brought before them, so that all might have access to them and those who came might be quickly dealt with. Hence it is commanded in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 16:18|Thou shalt appoint judges and magistrates in all thy gates|Judices constitues in portis urbium tuarum]] [Denis's wording: "Thou shalt appoint judges in the gates of thy cities"]. And holy Job: [[Job 29:7|When I went out|Procedebam]], he says, [[Job 29:7|to the gate of the city, and in the street they prepared me a chair?|ad portam civitatis, et in platea parabant cathedram mihi]]

paras.t: Usquequo, parvuli, diligitis infantiam? Per parvulos designantur quandoque humiles, in Scripturis (juxta illud Psalmistæ, Testimonium Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis ; et alibi, Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis); quandoque qui corpore parvi sunt (sicut de Christo fertur in Isaia, Parvulus natus est nobis ; atque in Evangelio, Sumens Jesus parvulum, statuit eum in medio) : interdum imperfecti (juxta illud Apostoli, Quum factus sum vir, evacuavi quæ erant parvuli); aliquando qui culpæ expertes sunt (prout Paulus hortatur, Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote); nonnunquam qui modicum habent de intellectu, prout Isaias asserit, Puer centum annorum morietur : et ita hic sumuntur. Infantia quoque primo accipitur pro infantia corporali. Secundo, pro simplicitate et innocentia, ut quum sacratissimus princeps Apostolorum in prima sua monet Canonica : Sicut modo geniti infantes rationabiles, sine dolo, lac concupiscite. Tertio, pro carnalitatis mollitie, et insolentia ac imperitia puerili : sicque accipitur hic, ut sit sensus : Quamdiu, o pusilli ac parvuli sensu, amatis carnalia et puerilia mala? Tales namque desuper illuminari non valent, sicut per Isaiam inducitur : Quem docebit Dominus scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere. Unde et scriptum est : Non invenitur sapientia in terra suaviter viventium.
paras.en: [[1:22|O children, how long will you love childishness|Usquequo, parvuli, diligitis infantiam]]? In the Scriptures "little ones" [parvuli, the word the Douay-Rheims here renders "children"] sometimes means the humble (according to that of the Psalmist, [[Ps 18:8|the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones|Testimonium Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis]]; and elsewhere, [[Matt 11:25|thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]); sometimes those who are small in body (as is said of Christ in Isaias, [[Is 9:6|a CHILD IS BORN to us|Parvulus natus est nobis]]; and in the Gospel, [[Matt 18:2|Jesus, calling unto him a little child, set him in the midst|Sumens Jesus parvulum, statuit eum in medio]]); at times the imperfect (according to that of the Apostle, [[1 Cor 13:11|when I became a man, I put away the things of a child|Quum factus sum vir, evacuavi quæ erant parvuli]]); at other times those who are free from guilt (as Paul exhorts, [[1 Cor 14:20|do not become children in sense. But in malice be children|Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote]]); and now and then those who have little understanding, as Isaias asserts, [[Is 65:20|the child shall die a hundred years old|Puer centum annorum morietur]]: and so it is taken here. Childishness [infantia, literally "infancy"], too, is taken first for bodily infancy. Secondly, for simplicity and innocence, as when the most holy prince of the Apostles admonishes in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes, desire the rational milk without guile|Sicut modo geniti infantes rationabiles, sine dolo, lac concupiscite]] [Denis reads rationabiles, so that "rational" goes with the babes, not with the milk]. Thirdly, for the softness of the flesh, and childish insolence and inexperience: and so it is taken here, so that the sense is: How long, O ye small ones and little ones in understanding, do you love carnal and childish evils? For such cannot be enlightened from above, as is brought in by Isaias: [[Is 28:9|Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing? them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts|Quem docebit Dominus scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere]]. Hence it is also written: [[Job 28:13|neither is it found in the land of them that live in delights|Non invenitur sapientia in terra suaviter viventium]].

paras.t: Et stulti ea quæ sibi sunt noxia, videlicet delectabilia, vana, illicita, cupient, et imprudentes, quibus deest discretio vera, ac virtus prudentiæ, odibunt scientiam salutarem, evangelicamque doctrinam, et informationem salubrem? Tales sunt, qui ignorantiam crassam habent, qui nolunt doceri, ut sine remorsu liberius peccent. Qui, ut ait Scriptura, quasi de industria recedunt a Deo. De quibus loquitur Job : Dixerunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus. O quam multi sunt tales, qui veram expositionem arctæ viæ salutis audire exhorrent, eosque diligunt a quibus complacentia suæ carnalitati vanitatique audiunt! De quibus Isaias: Dicunt adspicientibus : Nolite adspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt ; loquimini nobis placentia, videte nobis errores. Hinc Seneca in quarta ad Lucilium scribit epistola : Auctoritatem habemus senum, sed vitia puerorum, imo et infantium.
paras.en: [[1:22|and fools|Et stulti]] [[1:22|covet|cupient]] [[1:22|those things which are hurtful to themselves|ea quæ sibi sunt noxia]], namely things that are delightful, vain, unlawful; [[1:22|and the unwise|et imprudentes]], who lack true discernment and the virtue of prudence, [[1:22|hate knowledge|odibunt scientiam]], the knowledge of salvation, the teaching of the gospel and wholesome instruction? Such are those who have gross ignorance[[1 Cor 15:34||]] [ignorantia crassa, in the language of the schools: ignorance due to culpable neglect, which does not excuse], who will not be taught, so that they may sin more freely without remorse; who, as Scripture says, [[Job 34:27|as it were on purpose have revolted from him|quasi de industria recedunt a Deo]]. Of whom Job speaks: [[Job 21:14|have said to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways|Dixerunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus]] [the margin, cut off, reads only "xxi, 14"]. O how many there are such, who shrink from hearing the true exposition of the narrow way of salvation, and love those from whom they hear what pleases their carnality and vanity! Of whom Isaias says: [[Is 30:10|Who say|Dicunt]] [[Is 30:10|to them that behold: Behold not for us those things that are right: speak unto us pleasant things, see errors for us|adspicientibus : Nolite adspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt ; loquimini nobis placentia, videte nobis errores]]. Hence Seneca writes in his fourth epistle to Lucilius: We have the authority of old men, but the vices of boys, nay, even of infants.

paras.t: Convertimini ad correptionem meam, id est, verbis correptionis et castigationis meæ obtemperate, et dociles ac dirigibiles vos præbete. En proferam vobis spiritum meum, id est, animi mei conceptum, spiritualemque intellectum, seu Spiritum Sanctum vobis infundere sum paratus, dummodo quod in vobis est faciatis. Alia littera habet : Proferam vobis vindictam meam, id est, æternam damnationem prænuntiabo, ut vel ex timore cessetis peccare. Solet etenim spiritus pro indignatione, ira, seu ultione accipi in Scripturis, juxta illud in Job : Vidi iniquos Domino flante periisse, et spiritu iræ ejus esse consumptos. Et ostendam vobis verba mea ad vestram salutem spectantia.
paras.en: [[1:23|Turn ye at my reproof|Convertimini ad correptionem meam]], that is, obey the words of my reproof and chastisement, and show yourselves teachable and willing to be guided. [[1:23|behold I will utter my spirit to you|En proferam vobis spiritum meum]], that is, I am ready to pour into you the conception of my mind and spiritual understanding, or the Holy Ghost, provided you do what lies in you. Another reading has: I will utter my vengeance to you; that is, I will foretell eternal damnation, so that you may cease to sin, at least from fear. For "spirit" is often taken in the Scriptures for indignation, wrath or vengeance, according to that in Job: [[Job 4:8|I have seen|Vidi]] the wicked [[Job 4:9|Perishing by the blast of God, and consumed by the spirit of his wrath|Domino flante periisse, et spiritu iræ ejus esse consumptos]]. [[1:23|and will shew you my words|Et ostendam vobis verba mea]] that concern your salvation.

paras.t: Quia vocavi, id est, variis modis ad emendationem et pœnitentiam vos invitavi ac monui, per instinctum divinum, per angelicas inspirationes, per Apostolos et Prophetas, per prælatos et prædicatores, ac proximos virtuosos, et renuistis converti. Extendi manum meam, beneficia largiendo, et per adversa paterne castigando : hoc est, potestatem meam demonstravi in vobis per prospera et adversa : quatenus per prospera vos ad obsequium meum allicerem, et mea caritate accenderem ; aut per adversa terrerem et illustrarem, ita quod vexatio vobis intellectum conferret : juxta illud, Castigabo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius. Et Osee ait : Sepiam viam tuam spinis. Et non fuit qui adspiceret, id est, mentem suam ad me dirigeret, et visitationes præfatas attenderet : quemadmodum in Jeremia habetur, Induraverunt faciem suam supra petram, et noluerunt reverti.
paras.en: [[1:24|Because I called|Quia vocavi]], that is, I invited and admonished you in divers ways to amendment and penance: by divine prompting, by angelic inspirations, by the Apostles and Prophets, by prelates and preachers, and by virtuous neighbours; [[1:24|and you refused|et renuistis]] to be converted. [[1:24|I stretched out my hand|Extendi manum meam]], bestowing benefits, and chastising you like a father with adversities: that is, I showed my power in you by prosperity and adversity, so as to draw you to my service by prosperity and kindle you with my love, or else to frighten and enlighten you by adversity, so that vexation might give you understanding: according to that, [[Jer 30:11|I will chastise thee in judgment, that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent|Castigabo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius]]. And Osee says: [[Osee 2:6|I will hedge up thy way with thorns|Sepiam viam tuam spinis]]. [[1:24|and there was none that regarded|Et non fuit qui adspiceret]], that is, that turned his mind to me and heeded the visitations I have spoken of: as is said in Jeremias, [[Jer 5:3|they have made their faces harder than the rock, and they have refused to return|Induraverunt faciem suam supra petram, et noluerunt reverti]].

paras.t: Despexistis omne consilium meum, id est exhortationes quæ in divinis fiunt Scripturis, et consilia quæ dedi de vitandis occasionibus transgressionum, ac de operibus supererogationis, evangelica quoque consilia Christi. Unde Paulus disseruit : Non subterfugi, quominus annuntiarem vobis omne consilium Dei. Et increpationes meas, quibus per verba aut verbera redargui vitia vestra, neglexistis, non attendendo, aut velociter obliviscendo. De talibus incorrigibilibus et induratis diffuse loquitur Dominus : Dedi, inquiens, vobis stuporem dentium, et indigentiam panum, et prohibui a vobis imbrem, et percussi vos vento urente et aurugine ; et non redistis ad me.
paras.en: [[1:25|You have despised all my counsel|Despexistis omne consilium meum]], that is, the exhortations given in the divine Scriptures, and the counsels I gave about avoiding the occasions of transgression and about works of supererogation [that is, works beyond what is commanded], and also the gospel counsels of Christ. Hence Paul declared: [[Acts 20:27|I have not spread to declare unto you all, the counsel of God|Non subterfugi, quominus annuntiarem vobis omne consilium Dei]]. [[1:25|and have neglected|neglexistis]] [[1:25|my reprehensions|Et increpationes meas]], by which I rebuked your vices by words or by blows, by not heeding them or by quickly forgetting them. Of such incorrigible and hardened men the Lord speaks at length: [[Amos 4:6|I also have given|Dedi]], he says, [[Amos 4:6|you dulness of teeth|vobis stuporem dentium]], [[Amos 4:6|and want of bread|et indigentiam panum]], and [[Amos 4:7|I also have withholden the rain from you|prohibui a vobis imbrem]], and [[Amos 4:9|I struck you with a burning wind, and with mildew|percussi vos vento urente et aurugine]]; [[Amos 4:9|yet you returned not to me|et non redistis ad me]].

paras.t: Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, id est, per modum ridentis ac consolati habebo me in morte vestra, et in vestro particulari judicio ac condemnatione, exercendo in vobis cum gaudio effectum justitiæ meæ : juxta illud, Consolabor super hostibus meis, et vindicabor de inimicis meis. Et subsannabo : juxta sensum prætactum ; quum vobis id quod timebatis, advenerit, scilicet debita pœna pro culpis vestris. Hinc Dominus contestatur : Complebo furorem meum, et requiescere faciam indignationem meam, et consolabor. Hoc jam ante Salomonem pater ejus dixit in Psalmo : Qui habitat in cœlis, irridebit eos, et Dominus subsannabit eos. Tunc loquetur ad eos in ira sua, et in furore suo conturbabit eos.
paras.en: [[1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction|Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo]], that is, I will behave like one who laughs and is comforted at your death, and at your particular judgment and condemnation, carrying out in you with joy the effect of my justice: according to that, [[Is 1:24|I will comfort myself over my adversaries: and I will be revenged of my enemies|Consolabor super hostibus meis, et vindicabor de inimicis meis]]. [[1:26|and will mock|Et subsannabo]], in the sense just touched on; [[1:26|when that shall come to you which you feared|quum vobis id quod timebatis, advenerit]], namely the punishment due for your faults. Hence the Lord declares: [[Ezech 5:13|I will accomplish my fury, and will cause my indignation to rest upon them, and I will be comforted|Complebo furorem meum, et requiescere faciam indignationem meam, et consolabor]]. This his father had already said before Solomon, in the Psalm: [[Ps 2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: and the Lord shall deride them|Qui habitat in cœlis, irridebit eos, et Dominus subsannabit eos]]. [[Ps 2:5|Then shall he speak to them in his anger, and trouble them in his rage|Tunc loquetur ad eos in ira sua, et in furore suo conturbabit eos]].

paras.t: Quum irruerit repentina calamitas, id est improvisum periculum ac tormentum, et interitus quasi tempestas ingruerit : juxta illud in Psalmo : Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? Subito defecerunt ; perierunt propter iniquitatem suam. Quando venerit super vos tribulatio, et angustia cordis et corporis : quod præcipue fit in morte, quæ miris et ineffabilibus modis molestat, premit, ac tribulat morientem. Potest quoque istud referri ad horam extremi ac generalis judicii.
paras.en: [[1:27|When sudden calamity shall fall on you|Quum irruerit repentina calamitas]], that is, unforeseen danger and torment, [[1:27|and destruction, as a tempest, shall be at hand|et interitus quasi tempestas ingruerit]]: according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 72:19|How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: they have perished by reason of their iniquity|Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? Subito defecerunt ; perierunt propter iniquitatem suam]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxii, 27; the words are those of Ps 72:19]. [[1:27|when tribulation and distress shall come upon you|Quando venerit super vos tribulatio, et angustia]] of heart and body: which happens above all in death, which in wonderful and unspeakable ways troubles, presses and afflicts the dying. This can also be referred to the hour of the last and general judgment.

paras.t: Tunc invocabunt me, et non exaudiam. Multi enim in tempore mortis veniam petunt, nec obtinent ; confitentur, nec audiuntur : quia solo servili timore hæc faciunt, non zelo justitiæ. Post mortem quoque in particulari aut generali judicio, non patet precum aut veniæ locus, quando status viæ et tempus merendi sumpserint finem. Hinc de Antiocho fertur, quod orabat scelestus Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam consecuturus. Atque de Esau Apostolus ait : Non invenit pœnitentiæ locum, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam. Unde apud Isaiam Dominus loquitur : Quum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos ; et quum multiplicaveritis orationes, non exaudiam. Mane consurgent, id est, acerbitate pœnarum inducti, festinabunt me invocare, non amore virtutis ; vel, Mane consurgent, id est in die novissimo, quando resurgent alii in vitam, alii in opprobrium sempiternum ; et non invenient me sibi propitium, id est, misericordiam salvantem non impetrabunt, juxta illud : Opposuisti nubem tibi, ne transeat oratio.
paras.en: [[1:28|Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear|Tunc invocabunt me, et non exaudiam]]. For many ask for pardon at the time of death and do not obtain it; they confess and are not heard, because they do these things from servile fear alone [that is, fear of punishment only, not love of God], not from zeal for justice. After death, too, at the particular or the general judgment, there is no room for prayers or pardon, when the state of the way [that is, of this life, in which man is still a wayfarer] and the time of meriting have come to an end. Hence it is said of Antiochus that [[2 Mach 9:13|this wicked man prayed to the Lord, of whom he was not like to obtain mercy|scelestus Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam consecuturus]]. And the Apostle says of Esau: [[Heb 12:17|he found no place of repentance, although with tears he had sought it|Non invenit pœnitentiæ locum, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam]]. Hence the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 1:15|when you stretch forth your hands, I will turn away my eyes from you: and when you multiply prayer, I will not hear|Quum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos ; et quum multiplicaveritis orationes, non exaudiam]]. [[1:28|they shall rise in the morning|Mane consurgent]], that is, driven by the bitterness of their punishments they will make haste to call on me, not for love of virtue; or, [[1:28|they shall rise in the morning|Mane consurgent]], that is, on the last day, when some shall rise [[Dan 12:2|unto life everlasting, and others unto reproach|in vitam, alii in opprobrium sempiternum]]; [[1:28|and shall not find me|et non invenient me]] favourable to them, that is, they shall not obtain the mercy that saves, according to that: [[Lam 3:44|Thou hast set a cloud before thee, that our prayer may not pass through|Opposuisti nubem tibi, ne transeat oratio]].

paras.t: Eo quod exosam habuerint disciplinam, id est caritativam increpationem, justamque correctionem ; et timorem Domini initialem aut filialem, non susceperint, imo nec servilem, nec acquieverint consilio meo : sicut expositum est ; et detraxerint universæ correptioni meæ, sentiendo perverse de judiciis meis, aut corripientibus indignando ac obloquendo, ut scriptum est : Odio habuerunt in porta corripientem. De talibus Dominus ait per Zachariam : Noluerunt attendere, et averterunt scapulas recedentes, et cor suum posuerunt ut adamantem, ne audirent legem. De tam perversis hominibus conqueritur Deus in Numeris : Usquequo detrahet mihi populus iste ?
paras.en: [[1:29|Because they have hated instruction|Eo quod exosam habuerint disciplinam]], that is, loving rebuke and just correction; [[1:29|and received not|non susceperint]] [[1:29|the fear of the Lord|et timorem Domini]], initial or filial [the fear of a beginner, or the fear of a son], nay, not even servile fear; [[1:30|Nor consented to my counsel|nec acquieverint consilio meo]], as has been explained; [[1:30|but despised all my reproof|et detraxerint universæ correptioni meæ]] [detraxerint is literally "disparaged"], by thinking perversely of my judgments, or by being indignant with those who reprove them and speaking against them, as it is written: [[Amos 5:10|They have hated him that rebuketh in the gate|Odio habuerunt in porta corripientem]]. Of such the Lord says by Zacharias: [[Zach 7:11|they would not hearken, and they turned away the shoulder to depart|Noluerunt attendere, et averterunt scapulas recedentes]], [[Zach 7:12|And they made their heart as the adamant stone, lest they should hear the law|et cor suum posuerunt ut adamantem, ne audirent legem]]. Of men so perverse God complains in Numbers: [[Num 14:11|How long will this people detract me|Usquequo detrahet mihi populus iste]]?

paras.t: Comedent igitur fructus viæ suæ, id est, justa retributione suæ perversitatis implebuntur, et quasi reficientur ut cibo, quemadmodum ait Psalmista : Sicut oves […] suisque consiliis saturabuntur, id est, effectu ac præmiatione miserrima et pœnosa suorum perversorum replebuntur consiliorum.
paras.en: [[1:31|Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way|Comedent igitur fructus viæ suæ]], that is, they shall be filled with the just requital of their perversity, and fed with it as with food, as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 48:15|like sheep|Sicut oves]] […] [text lost in the transcription at the foot of the column; the margin gives Ps. xlviii, 15, "They are laid in hell like sheep"] [[1:31|and shall be filled with their own devices|suisque consiliis saturabuntur]], that is, they shall be filled with the most wretched and painful effect and reward of their perverse counsels.

paras.t: Aversio parvulorum sensu : de quibus jam dictum est, Usquequo, parvuli, diligitis infantiam ? Interficiet eos. Tales etenim a Deo aversi sunt corde, præponendo caritati ipsius affectionem ad transitoria atque carnalia. Et hæc ipsa aversio, occidit eorum animas spirituali interitu : imo est mors culpæ, et mortale peccatum, quo spiritualiter coram Deo sunt mortui. De qua morte ait Salvator : Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos. Et in Apocalypsi : Nomen habes quod vivas, sed mortuus es. Hæc quoque aversio, post hanc vitam ocidet eos morte damnationis æternæ, secundum illud : Pars illorum erit in stagno ardenti igne et sulfure, quod est mors secunda. Et prosperitas stultorum perdet illos : id est, terrena prosperatio impiorum, qua in præsenti sæculo consequuntur divitias, delicias et honores, erit causa sive occasio perditionis eorum perpetuæ in futuro : quoniam abutuntur beneficiis Dei, et extolluntur ex prosperitate præsenti. De quibus ait Psalmographus : Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua, imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges. De quibus Job : Impii sublevati sunt, confortatique divitiis, et non est virga Dei super eos ; ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad infernum descendunt.
paras.en: [[1:32|The turning away of little ones|Aversio parvulorum]] in understanding, of whom it has already been said: [[1:22|O children, how long will you love childishness|Usquequo, parvuli, diligitis infantiam]]? [[1:32|shall kill them|Interficiet eos]]. For such men are turned away from God in heart, preferring affection for passing and carnal things to the love of him. And this very turning away kills their souls with a spiritual death: indeed it is the death of guilt, and mortal sin, by which they are spiritually dead before God. Of which death the Saviour says: [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]]. And in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:1|thou hast the name of being alive. And thou art dead|Nomen habes quod vivas, sed mortuus es]]. This turning away also, after this life, will kill them with the death of eternal damnation, according to that: [[Apoc 21:8|they shall have their portion in the pool burning with fire and brimstone, which is the second death|Pars illorum erit in stagno ardenti igne et sulfure, quod est mors secunda]]. [[1:32|and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them|Et prosperitas stultorum perdet illos]]: that is, the earthly prosperity of the wicked, by which in the present world they obtain riches, pleasures and honours, will be the cause or occasion of their everlasting perdition in the world to come, because they abuse the gifts of God and are puffed up by present prosperity. Of whom the Psalmist says: [[Ps 72:20|As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.|Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua, imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges]]. Of whom Job: The wicked are [[Job 21:7|advanced, and strengthened with riches|sublevati sunt, confortatique divitiis]], [[Job 21:9|and the rod of God is not upon them|et non est virga Dei super eos]]; [[Job 21:13|They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell|ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad infernum descendunt]].

paras.t: Insuper potest et ita exponi : Aversio parvulorum interficiet eos, scilicet impios, de quibus prædictum est : qui ex aversione parvulorum et prosperitate stultorum, qui in vita hac videntur impune peccare, imo peccando etiam prosperari, scandalizantur, et sumunt peccandi occasionem atque audaciam, deserentes viam justitiæ. Quocontra ait Propheta : Noli æmulari in malignantibus, neque zelaveris facientes iniquitatem, quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent. In Job quoque ait vir istud perpendens : Ego vidi impium firma radice, et maledixi pulchritudini ejus. Et de viro justo fertur in Psalmo : Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus. Sapientes namque et justi, intuentes impiorum prosperitatem, pro nihilo reputant eos, ut tales, et compatiuntur eisdem, certi hoc periculosissimum esse, peccare, et nihilo minus prosperari, nec in præsenti sæculo castigari.
paras.en: Moreover it can also be explained thus: [[1:32|The turning away of little ones shall kill them|Aversio parvulorum interficiet eos]], namely the wicked, of whom we spoke before: who are scandalized at the turning away of little ones and the prosperity of fools, who seem in this life to sin unpunished, nay, even to prosper by sinning; and so they take occasion and boldness to sin, forsaking the way of justice. Against this the Prophet says: [[Ps 36:1|Be not emulous of evildoers; nor envy them that work iniquity|Noli æmulari in malignantibus, neque zelaveris facientes iniquitatem]], [[Ps 36:2|For they shall shortly wither away as grass|quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent]]. In Job too a man weighing this says: [[Job 5:3|I have seen a fool with a strong root, and I cursed his beauty|Ego vidi impium firma radice, et maledixi pulchritudini ejus]] [Denis reads impium, "the wicked man", where the Vulgate has "a fool"]. And of the just man it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]] [the margin, cut off, reads only "xiv, 4"]. For the wise and the just, seeing the prosperity of the wicked, count them as nothing, as such men are, and have compassion on them, being sure that this is most perilous: to sin and nevertheless to prosper, and not to be chastised in this present world.

paras.t: Qui autem me audierit auribus mentis, id est, obtemperaverit jussionibus meis, absque terrore quiescet : id est, pacem pectoris possidebit, et constans et securus erit in Deo, omni inordinata exclusa formidine, nec turbabitur, sed gloriabitur in adversis; et demum post vitam hanc, pace æternitatis feliciter erit plenus. Et abundantia perfruetur : quia nunc in donis gratiæ, deinde in bonis gloriæ abundabit, et possidebit bona Domini in regione vivorum, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt ; malorum terrore sublato, ita quod mala ultra non formidabit. Nempe, in vita præsenti erit paratus ad mala pœnæ propter Deum et suam salutem æquanimiter toleranda, sicut et infra habetur : Justus quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit. In patria autem, nec mala pœnæ, nec mala culpæ possunt accidere. Hinc in Isaia loquitur Dominus : Erit opus justitiæ, pax ; et cultus justitiæ, silentium, et securitas usque in sempiternum ; et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta.
paras.en: [[1:33|But he that shall hear me|Qui autem me audierit]] with the ears of the mind, that is, shall obey my commands, [[1:33|shall rest without terror|absque terrore quiescet]]: that is, he shall possess peace of heart, and be steadfast and secure in God, all disordered fear being shut out; he shall not be troubled, but shall glory in adversities; and at last, after this life, he shall be happily filled with the peace of eternity. [[1:33|and shall enjoy abundance|Et abundantia perfruetur]]: because now in the gifts of grace, and afterwards in the goods of glory, he shall abound, and shall possess [[Ps 26:13|the good things of the Lord in the land of the living|bona Domini in regione vivorum]], which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man|nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis]][[Is 64:4||]] [the margins, partly cut off, read "xxvi, 13", "lxiv, 4" and "Cor. ii, 9"]; [[1:33|without fear of evils|malorum terrore sublato]], so that he shall no longer dread evils. For in the present life he will be ready to bear with an even mind the evils of punishment for God's sake and for his own salvation, as is also said below: [[Prov 28:1|the just, bold as a lion, shall be without dread|Justus quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit]]. But in the fatherland [that is, in heaven] neither the evils of punishment nor the evils of guilt can befall. Hence the Lord speaks in Isaias: [[Is 32:17|the work of justice shall be peace, and the service of justice quietness, and security for ever|Erit opus justitiæ, pax ; et cultus justitiæ, silentium, et securitas usque in sempiternum]]; [[Is 32:18|And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]].

paras.t: Postremo, quidquid hic dictum est de justo et impiis, referri potest ad Christum et Judæos persecutores ipsius, discipulorumque ejus : quibus impii perfidique Judæi inaniter posuerunt insidias, rete atque decipulas; imo hoc faciendo, sibimetipsis mercati sunt finalem istam captivitatem, et condemnationem æternam. Quos Christus et ejus Apostoli multipliciter docuerunt, pie corripuerunt, et de æterna eorum calamitate præmonuerunt; extenderunt etiam manus suas ad ipsos, faciendo multa et præclara miracula. Imo et in cruce extendit Salvator manus pro eis, sicut per Isaiam testatur : Tota die extendi manus meas ad populum non credentem. Ipsi vero parvuli sensu, dilexerunt infantiam, id est rudimenta et superficiem legis, quæ fuit pædagogus noster in Christo ; sibique noxia cupierunt, scilicet perpetuam cæremonialium observantiam præceptorum, et oderunt summam evangelicæ legis scientiam. Ideo Christus tandem fecit Apostolos ab eis induratis recedere, ac gentibus prædicare ; et in eorum risit interitu, eosque ex zelo justitiæ subsannavit, ac hostibus tradidit, sicut per Isaiam Dominus prædixerat : Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea. Quumque irruisset super eos repentina obsidio a Romanis, vastitasque gravissima, fames, pestis, venditio, interfectio millium plurimorum, reliquit eos omnino ; nec eorum sacrificia, orationes, fletus ac gemitus exaudivit Altissimus, eo quod exosam habuerunt Christi disciplinam ac legem : tuncque perfidiarum et impietatum suarum, ac pravissimorum consiliorum fructus et demerita invenerunt ac perceperunt. De hac expositione transeo, quia facillimum est litteram applicare ad eam.
paras.en: Lastly, whatever has been said here of the just man and the wicked can be referred to Christ and the Jews who persecuted him and his disciples: for whom the wicked and faithless Jews laid snares, the net and traps, in vain; nay, by doing so they bought for themselves this final captivity and eternal condemnation. These Christ and his Apostles taught in many ways, reproved with love, and forewarned of their eternal calamity; they also stretched out their hands to them, working many and glorious miracles. Nay, on the cross too the Saviour stretched out his hands for them, as he testifies by Isaias: [[Is 65:2|I have spread forth my hands all the day to an unbelieving people|Tota die extendi manus meas ad populum non credentem]]. But they, little ones in understanding, loved childishness, that is, the rudiments and surface of the law, which [[Gal 3:24|was our pedagogue in Christ|fuit pædagogus noster in Christo]]; and they coveted what was hurtful to them, namely the perpetual observance of the ceremonial precepts, and hated the highest knowledge of the law of the gospel. Therefore Christ at last made the Apostles depart from them, hardened as they were, and preach to the gentiles[[Acts 13:46||]]; and he laughed at their destruction, and in zeal for justice mocked them and delivered them to their enemies, as the Lord had foretold by Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]]. And when the sudden siege by the Romans fell upon them, and the most grievous devastation, famine, pestilence, selling into slavery, the slaughter of many thousands, he forsook them utterly; and the Most High did not hear their sacrifices, prayers, weeping and groaning, because they hated the discipline and law of Christ: and then they found and received the fruit and the deserts of their faithlessness and impieties and most wicked counsels. I pass over this exposition, because it is very easy to fit the letter to it.

paras.t: Nos itaque Christum in omnibus audiamus, quatenus omni nostra affectione et intentione simplificatis ac fixis in Deo, omnique nostra occupatione secundum divinam legem directa, atque in Deum frequenter relata, quiescamus in Creatore absque omni vitioso et infructuoso timore, ac per hoc in divinorum opulentia charismatum proficiamus et abundemus assidue.
paras.en: Let us therefore hear Christ in all things, so that, with all our affection and intention made simple and fixed on God, and all our occupation directed according to the divine law and often referred to God, we may rest in the Creator without any vicious and fruitless fear, and thereby make progress and abound continually in the riches of the divine gifts.

2.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : FILI MI, SI SUSCEPERIS SERMONES MEOS.
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: My son, if thou wilt receive my words.

paras.t: Dicunt nonnulli, quod postquam Salomon præcedenti capitulo docuit vitare avaritiam, hic nunc docet vitare idololatriam : quod non videtur idonee dictum, quia nec in isto capitulo videtur ad litteram de idololatria mentio fieri, ut patebit ; nec in præcedenti capitulo solum aut principaliter contra avaritiam est tractatum, sed ostensum est ibi, quid ad sapientem intelligentemque pertineat. Deinde fit ibi monitio, ne quis peccatorum blanditiis seducatur ad committendum homicidium aut rapinam ; et qualiter transgressores plus noceant sibi ipsis, quam aliis. Deinceps introducitur ibi, qualiter summa et increata Sapientia increpet et præmoneat insipientes atque injustos, et quam fructuosum sit Deo in omnibus obedire.
paras.en: Some say that, after Solomon in the preceding chapter taught us to shun avarice, here he now teaches us to shun idolatry. This does not seem fitly said: for neither does this chapter seem to make any mention of idolatry according to the letter, as will appear; nor was the preceding chapter only or chiefly directed against avarice. Rather, it was shown there what belongs to the wise and understanding man. Then a warning was given there, that no one be led on by the blandishments of sinners to commit murder or robbery; and how transgressors harm themselves more than others. After that it was brought in how the supreme and uncreated Wisdom rebukes and forewarns the foolish and unjust, and how fruitful it is to obey God in all things.

paras.t: His igitur ibi peractis, hic rursus hortatur ad sapientiam amplectendam, et quanto affectu sit exquirenda, quanta etiam bona homo ex ejus acquisitione ac possessione consequatur. Quum etenim nemo sit sapientiæ hujus capax, nisi purgatus a vitiis, recte in præcedenti capitulo ad cordis expurgationem hortatus est : et admonitionem de sapientia obtinenda ibi inchoatam, hoc loco prosequitur.
paras.en: These things done there, here he exhorts us again to embrace wisdom, and shows with what affection it is to be sought out, and what great goods a man gains from acquiring and possessing it. For since no one is capable of this wisdom unless he has been cleansed of vices, he rightly exhorted us in the preceding chapter to the cleansing of the heart; and the admonition about obtaining wisdom begun there he carries on in this place.

paras.t: Fili mi, si susceperis sermones meos, diligenter eos audiendo, considerando, ac recolendo, et mandata mea absconderis penes te, id est, in fundo cordis tui sollicite reposueris, ne per oblivionem, aut negligentiam violes ea. Juxta quem sensum ait Propheta : In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. Econtra de quibusdam ait in Evangelio Dominus, quod quum receperint semen verbi cœlestis, volucres cœli, id est aeriæ potestates, devorant illud, id est, infructuosum efficiunt. Verumtamen, non sic abscondenda sunt mandata ac verba Dei in corde, ut publice non impleantur nec aliis communicentur, quum dicat Salvator : Luceat lux vestra coram hominibus. Princeps quoque Apostolorum : Unusquisque, inquit, sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes. Et item Joannes in Apocalypsi : Qui audit, dicat, Veni : hoc est, qui mandata Dei audierit, proximum suum invitet ad eadem peragenda.
paras.en: [[2:1|My son, if thou wilt receive my words|Fili mi, si susceperis sermones meos]], by hearing them diligently, pondering them and going over them again, [[2:1|and wilt hide my commandments with thee|et mandata mea absconderis penes te]], that is, wilt carefully lay them up in the depth of thy heart, lest through forgetfulness or negligence thou break them. In this sense the Prophet says: [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi]]. On the other hand, the Lord says in the Gospel of certain men that when they have received the seed of the heavenly word, the birds of the air, that is, the powers of the air, devour it[[Matt 13:4||]], that is, make it fruitless[[Matt 13:19||]]. Yet the commandments and words of God are not to be so hidden in the heart that they are not fulfilled openly or shared with others, since the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:16|let your light shine before men|Luceat lux vestra coram hominibus]]. And the Prince of the Apostles: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man|Unusquisque]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:10|hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]]. And again John in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:17|he that heareth, let him say: Come|Qui audit, dicat, Veni]]: that is, whoever has heard the commandments of God, let him invite his neighbour to carry them out.

paras.t: Ut audiat sapientiam, id est sapientialia verba, auris tua corporalis ac spiritualis, puta auditus et intellectus. Inclina cor tuum, id est, intellectum tuum cum humilitate ac diligentia applica, ad cognoscendam prudentiam, id est sapientiam, sumendo prudentiæ nomen extense ; vel, Ad cognoscendam prudentiam, quæ est virtus moralis ac cardinalis, rectaque ratio agibilium, id est virtus et habitus, per quem homo cognoscit quid agere, quid omittere debeat in rebus quæ ei occurrunt, prout Ethicorum sexto habetur. Itaque ait, Inclina cor tuum ad cognoscendam prudentiam : quia non sufficit cognitio divinorum, sed humanorum quoque actuum et negotiorum notitia vera ac discreta requiritur : et ne quis ex divinorum agnitione se erigens, aspernetur etiam inferiora addiscere.
paras.en: [[2:2|That thy ear may hearken to wisdom|Ut audiat sapientiam]], that is, to words of wisdom: [[2:2|thy ear|auris tua]], bodily and spiritual, namely the hearing and the understanding. [[2:2|incline thy heart|Inclina cor tuum]], that is, apply thy understanding with humility and diligence, [[2:2|to know prudence|ad cognoscendam prudentiam]], that is, wisdom, taking the word *prudence* in a broad sense; or, to know prudence, which is a moral and cardinal virtue, and right reason about things to be done [*recta ratio agibilium*]: that is, the virtue and habit by which a man knows what he ought to do and what to leave undone in the matters that come before him, as is said in the sixth book of the *Ethics*. So he says, Incline thy heart to know prudence, because the knowledge of divine things is not enough: a true and discerning knowledge of human acts and affairs is also required; and also lest anyone, puffed up by his knowledge of divine things, should disdain to learn lower things as well.

paras.t: Denique, ad acquirendum tam sapientiam quam prudentiam, cum humilitate et diligentia oportet accedere. Nam sicut in vallibus colliguntur aquarum fluenta, ita in cordibus humilium superna charismata, aqua sapientiæ, virtus prudentiæ, lumen scientiæ. Atque, ut in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Auris bona audiet cum omni concupiscentia sapientiam.
paras.en: Lastly, to acquire both wisdom and prudence one must come with humility and diligence. For as the streams of waters gather in the valleys, so the gifts from on high gather in the hearts of the humble: the water of wisdom, the virtue of prudence, the light of knowledge. And, as is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:31|a good ear will hear wisdom with all desire|Auris bona audiet cum omni concupiscentia sapientiam]].

paras.t: Hinc consequenter ostenditur, quam instanter ac fervide sapientia sit quærenda. Si enim sapientiam invocaveris, id est, orando vocaveris eam in te, et increatam Sapientiam suppliciter fueris deprecatus, ut animam tuam radio sapientiæ salutaris perfundat ac impleat, et pro infusione et incremento, ac conservatione sapientiæ rogaveris Dominum incessanter ; et inclinaveris cor tuum prudentiæ. Si quæsieris eam quasi pecuniam, id est tam indesinenter et insatiabiliter, tam laboriose ac fervide, sicut cupidus quærit argentum et aurum : de quibus quanto plus obtinet, tanto plus cupit ac quærit, diligentiusque custodit hæc acquisita ; et sicut thesauros effoderis illam, id est, ex fonte sapientiæ studueris eam haurire tali instantia et ardore, sicut quis thesaurum in terra absconditum nititur invenire terram effodiendo. Circa hoc ait Glossa : Qui thesauros effodit, terram rejicit, et foveam facit profundam, sedulo insistens, donec quod quærit, inveniat : sic qui thesauros sapientiæ desiderat invenire, omne pondus terrenum a se rejiciat, et foveam humilitatis faciat in se, nec quiescat, donec inveniat. Denique huic simile est quod Seneca in suis ait Proverbiis : Ut auri aliquid extrahamus, terram evertimus : ut summum bonum occupemus, et sapientiam reperiamus, pectus scrutari piget ?
paras.en: Next it is shown how urgently and fervently wisdom is to be sought. [[2:3|For if thou shalt call for wisdom|Si enim sapientiam invocaveris]], that is, shalt call her into thee by praying, and shalt humbly beseech the uncreated Wisdom to flood and fill thy soul with the ray of saving wisdom, and shalt ask the Lord unceasingly for the infusion, the increase and the keeping of wisdom; [[2:3|and incline thy heart to prudence|et inclinaveris cor tuum prudentiæ]]. [[2:4|If thou shalt seek her as money|Si quæsieris eam quasi pecuniam]], that is, as ceaselessly and insatiably, as laboriously and fervently as the covetous man seeks silver and gold: of which the more he gets, the more he desires and seeks, and the more carefully he guards what he has gained; [[2:4|and shalt dig for her as for a treasure|et sicut thesauros effoderis illam]], that is, shalt strive to draw her from the fountain of wisdom with such urgency and ardour as a man uses who tries to find a treasure hidden in the earth by digging up the ground. On this the Gloss says: He who digs for treasure throws out the earth and makes a deep pit, keeping steadily at it until he finds what he seeks; so let him who desires to find the treasures of wisdom throw off from himself every earthly weight, and make in himself the pit of humility, and not rest until he finds. Like this, finally, is what Seneca says in his *Proverbs*: To get out a little gold we turn the earth upside down; to lay hold of the highest good and find wisdom, are we loath to search our own breast?

paras.t: Tunc intelliges timorem Domini, id est, vere experimentaliterque cognosces, atque in te invenies filialem Dei timorem. Quanto namque intentius studueris desuper illustrari et dono sapientiæ perfici, tanto amplius formidabis summi Dei Patris adspectum offendere, et coram eo intimorate te gerere ; ipsaque infusa sapientia te docebit istum timorem castum et sanctum, ostendendo tibi quam infinite et incomparabiliter Deus altissimus sit sincere timendus, honorandus, ac diligendus : sicque ingeret tibi sapientialem pudorem, ut ubique erubescas coram divini vultus præsentia inhoneste, negligenter, aut turpiter te habere. Ad quod etiam Seneca admonens, ait : Non aliter te habeas in secreto, aliter in publico. Et scientiam Dei invenies, id est, sapientiam ejusque profectum et perfectionem obtinebis a Domino. De quo Psalmista : Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini ; et facies vestræ non confundentur. De qua scientia dicit Dominus in Osee : Scientiam Dei volo plus quam holocausta. Apostolus quoque ad Philippenses : Existimo, inquit, omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Per hanc demum infusam seu acquisitam Dei scientiam, aliqualiter invenimus, cognoscimus et contemplamur increatam Dei scientiam : de qua in libro de Mirabili scientia Dei sublimiter tractat Albertus Magnus.
paras.en: [[2:5|Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord|Tunc intelliges timorem Domini]], that is, thou shalt truly and by experience know, and find in thyself, the filial fear of God. For the more earnestly thou strivest to be enlightened from above and perfected by the gift of wisdom, the more shalt thou dread to offend the sight of God the Father most high, and to bear thyself before him without fear; and this infused wisdom itself will teach thee that chaste and holy fear, showing thee how infinitely and incomparably the most high God is to be sincerely feared, honoured and loved. And so it will put into thee a wise shame, so that everywhere thou wilt blush to behave unbecomingly, carelessly or basely in the presence of the divine countenance. Seneca too counsels this when he says: Do not conduct thyself one way in private and another in public. [[2:5|and shalt find the knowledge of God|Et scientiam Dei invenies]], that is, thou shalt obtain from the Lord wisdom, and progress and perfection in it. Of which the Psalmist says: [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened: and your faces shall not be confounded|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini ; et facies vestræ non confundentur]]. Of this knowledge the Lord says in Osee that he wills [[Osee 6:6|the knowledge of God more than holocausts|Scientiam Dei volo plus quam holocausta]]. The Apostle also, to the Philippians: [[Phil 3:8|I count|Existimo]], he says, [[Phil 3:8|all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. Through this knowledge of God, infused or acquired, we in some manner find, know and contemplate the uncreated knowledge of God, of which Albert the Great treats sublimely in his book *On the Wonderful Knowledge of God*.

paras.t: Quia Dominus dat sapientiam his, qui modo prætacto eam exquirunt. Sapientia autem quæ est donum Spiritus Sancti, a solo Deo immediate datur, et per creationem infunditur ; sapientia vero quæ est donum gratiæ gratis datæ, et sapientia naturalis, quandoque etiam infunduntur immediate a Deo, quandoque etiam dantur a Deo mediate, videlicet per studium et laborem, per informationem angelicam vel humanam. Nam omne bonum a Deo est, procedit, confertur. Et ex ore ejus prudentia, de qua dictum est, et scientia derivantur ac profluunt : sive scientia accipiatur pro dono gratiæ gratum facientis, quod est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, et a Deo solum immediate infunditur ; sive accipiatur prout est donum gratiæ gratis datæ, de qua Paulus, Alii, inquit, datur sermo sapientiæ, alii sermo scientiæ ; sive ut est unus de quinque habitibus intellectualibus, puta habitus naturalis et acquisitus, qui tamen potest a Deo supernaturaliter dari : de qua scientia sexto Ethicorum tractatur ; estque notitia eorum quæ aliter nequeunt se habere, videlicet recta ratio speculandorum.
paras.en: [[2:6|Because the Lord giveth wisdom|Quia Dominus dat sapientiam]] to those who seek her out in the way just described. Now the wisdom that is a gift of the Holy Ghost is given by God alone, immediately, and is infused by creation; but the wisdom that is a gift of grace freely given [*gratia gratis data*: a grace given for the good of others, such as prophecy or the word of wisdom, as distinct from sanctifying grace], and natural wisdom, are sometimes also infused immediately by God, and sometimes given by God mediately, namely through study and labour, and through the instruction of angels or of men. For every good is from God, proceeds from him and is bestowed by him. [[2:6|and out of his mouth cometh prudence|Et ex ore ejus prudentia]], of which we have spoken, [[2:6|and knowledge|et scientia]] are derived and flow forth: whether knowledge be taken for the gift of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God], which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost and is infused immediately by God alone; or be taken as a gift of grace freely given, of which Paul says: [[1 Cor 12:8|To one indeed|Alii]], he says, [[1 Cor 12:8|is given the word of wisdom|datur sermo sapientiæ]]; [[1 Cor 12:8|and to another, the word of knowledge|alii sermo scientiæ]]; or as one of the five intellectual habits, namely a natural and acquired habit, which nevertheless can be given by God supernaturally: of which knowledge [*scientia*] the sixth book of the *Ethics* treats, and it is the knowledge of things that cannot be otherwise, that is, right reason about things to be contemplated.

paras.t: Porro os Dei est increata sapientia et æternus intellectus ipsius, quo intra se profert Verbum æternum. Quandoque tamen os Domini appellantur Scripturæ sanctæ, seu ipsi Prophetæ : quoniam ex Scripturis datur nobis instructio atque responsio. Unde scriptum est : Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit. Per Prophetas quoque et Sanctos suos respondet quærentibus. Propter quod ipse per Prophetam ait : Væ, filii desertores, ut faceretis consilium, et non ex me ; et os meum non interrogastis. Hinc alibi protestatur : Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris. Postulanda est ergo semper divina directio, et sapientia desuper est quærenda : quæ nihilo minus ex ore doctorum, et libris, quantum fieri potest, est accipienda. Ideo scriptum est : Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et non improperat ; et dabitur ei.
paras.en: Further, the mouth of God is his uncreated wisdom and his eternal intellect, by which he utters within himself the eternal Word. Sometimes, however, the holy Scriptures, or the Prophets themselves, are called the mouth of the Lord, since from the Scriptures instruction and answer are given us. Hence it is written: [[Job 33:14|God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time|Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit]]. Through the Prophets also and his Saints he answers those who seek. Wherefore he himself says through the Prophet: [[Is 30:1|Woe to you, apostate children|Væ, filii desertores]], [[Is 30:1|that you would take counsel, and not of me|ut faceretis consilium, et non ex me]]; and you [[Is 30:2|have not asked at my mouth|os meum non interrogastis]]. Hence elsewhere he declares: If [[Jer 15:19|thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth|separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris]]. Divine direction, then, is always to be asked for, and wisdom sought from above; and none the less it is to be received, as far as may be, from the mouth of teachers and from books. Therefore it is written: [[Jas 1:5|if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God who giveth to all men abundantly and upbraideth not. And it shall be given him|Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et non improperat ; et dabitur ei]].

paras.t: Custodiet Dominus rectorum salutem, id est, justos in eorum salute conservabit. Habetur enim in hac vita salus seu beatitudo in quadam inchoatione, prælibatione, merito et spe. Unde in Matthæo ponuntur octo beatitudines, quæ sunt virtutum excellentium actiones et merita, per quæ pervenitur ad salutem regni cælestis completam. Nam dicitur ibi : Beati pauperes spiritu, etc. Dum ergo Omnipotens justos conservat in actibus virtuosis, custodit rectorum salutem. Nempe a Deo est inceptio, continuatio et consummatio, prosecutio et custoditio omnis boni. Aliqui tamen recti interdum ex propria negligentia dilabuntur in culpam, fiuntque miseri calamitate peccati : de qua in Apocalypsi dicitur, Nescis quia tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus ? Et proteget gradientes simpliciter, id est eos qui in columbina simplicitate serviunt ei, exclusa omni duplicitate, simulatione, hypocrisi. Tales etenim præcipue placent Deo, qui est simplicissimus in natura, uniformis, invariabilis, et unicus in operatione, ut in fine tangitur septimi Ethicorum. Hinc Job vir simplex et rectus placuit valde Deo. Ideo Christus : Estote, inquit, simplices sicut columbæ. Et primo Paralipomenon fatetur David : Scio, Domine, quod simplicitatem diligas.
paras.en: [[2:7|He wilt keep the salvation of the righteous|Custodiet Dominus rectorum salutem]], namely the Lord: that is, he will preserve the just in their salvation. For in this life salvation or beatitude is had in a kind of beginning, a foretaste, in merit and in hope. Hence in Matthew eight beatitudes are set down, which are the acts and merits of excellent virtues, by which one comes to the complete salvation of the heavenly kingdom; for it is said there: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit|Beati pauperes spiritu]], etc. So while the Almighty preserves the just in virtuous acts, he keeps the salvation of the righteous. For from God are the beginning, the continuance and the completion, the carrying on and the keeping of every good. Yet some righteous men at times slip into sin through their own negligence, and become wretched by the calamity of sin, of which it is said in the Apocalypse: Thou [[Apoc 3:17|knowest not that thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|Nescis quia tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus]]? [[2:7|and protect them that walk in simplicity|Et proteget gradientes simpliciter]], that is, those who serve him in dovelike simplicity, all duplicity, pretence and hypocrisy shut out. For such men chiefly please God, who is most simple in nature, uniform, unchangeable and one in his working, as is touched on at the end of the seventh book of the *Ethics*. Hence Job, [[Job 2:3|a man simple and upright|vir simplex et rectus]], greatly pleased God[[Job 1:1||]]. Therefore Christ says: [[Matt 10:16|Be ye|Estote]], he says, [[Matt 10:16|simple as doves|simplices sicut columbæ]]. And in the first book of Paralipomenon David confesses: [[1 Par 29:17|I know|Scio]], O Lord, that thou [[1 Par 29:17|lovest simplicity|simplicitatem diligas]].

paras.t: Simplices ergo, quorum intentio est recta, et cor sincerum coram Altissimo, ita quod ei soli, et aliis non nisi in ipso cupiunt complacere, proteguntur a Creatore, ne tentationibus seducantur, aut adversitatibus opprimantur. Sine hac simplicitate nullus est justus ; nec justus est qui hac simplicitate caret. Ideo, teste Glossa, simplicitas et rectitudo inseparabiliter sunt connexæ. Propter quod asserit Beda : Simplicitas sine rectitudine, est dissoluta, laxa et stulta ; rectitudo vero sine simplicitate, dura est et austera. Est autem et alia simplicitas asinina, quæ per exclusionem prudentiæ sic vocatur, et displicet Deo.
paras.en: The simple, then, whose intention is right and whose heart is sincere before the Most High, so that they desire to please him alone, and others only in him, are protected by the Creator, lest they be led astray by temptations or crushed by adversities. Without this simplicity no one is just; nor is he just who lacks this simplicity. Therefore, as the Gloss witnesses, simplicity and uprightness are inseparably joined. For which reason Bede asserts: Simplicity without uprightness is dissolute, slack and foolish; uprightness without simplicity is hard and austere. There is also another, asinine simplicity, so called because it shuts out prudence; and it displeases God.

paras.t: Servans semitas justitiæ, id est in esse conservans opera justa, et vias sanctorum, id est actiones ac merita perfectorum, custodiens, ne a regia via discedant. Possunt quoque per semitam consilia designari, per viam, mandata : quæ omnia Dominus tunc custodit, dum homini gratiam perseverantiæ ac circumspectionis tribuit, per quam Deo auxiliante custodit se ipsum in actibus bonis.
paras.en: [[2:8|Keeping the paths of justice|Servans semitas justitiæ]], that is, keeping just works in being, and [[2:8|the ways of saints|et vias sanctorum]], that is, the deeds and merits of the perfect, [[2:8|guarding|custodiens]], lest they depart from the king's highway. By the *path* the counsels may also be meant, and by the *way* the commandments: all of which the Lord keeps when he gives a man the grace of perseverance and of circumspection, by which, with God's help, he keeps himself in good acts.

paras.t: Tunc intelliges justitiam, id est, quid sit virtus justitiæ scies, non nuda et informis notitia, sed cognitione formata : ita quod justus eris, et per connaturalitatem gustumque mentis, bene de ipsa justitia judicabis, pensando et adimplendo quod spectat ad eam : quemadmodum habens non solum notitiam ethicæ, sed etiam ipsas virtutes morales, multo melius judicat de virtutibus illis, quam qui solam nudam scholasticamque notitiam habet de ipsis. Simili modo intelliges et judicium discretionis : quod est actus prudentiæ, quo inter bonum et malum discernitur ; et item judicium, id est prolationem justæ sententiæ : quod est actus justitiæ spectans ad judicem, cujus est justam in omni causa proferre determinationem ; et æquitatem, id est justitiam contemperatam clementiæ ex vera discretione, et omnem semitam bonam, id est virtuosam actionem, quæ ad ultimum finem recte deducit.
paras.en: [[2:9|Then shalt thou understand justice|Tunc intelliges justitiam]], that is, thou shalt know what the virtue of justice is, not with a bare and unformed knowledge but with a formed knowledge [that is, knowledge quickened by charity and practice, as faith is called *formed* by charity]: so that thou shalt be just, and through connaturality and the mind's taste thou shalt judge well of justice itself, weighing and fulfilling what belongs to it; just as one who has not only the knowledge of ethics but the moral virtues themselves judges of those virtues much better than one who has only a bare, scholastic knowledge of them. In like manner thou shalt understand [[2:9|and judgment|et judicium]] of discernment, which is an act of prudence, by which good and evil are distinguished; and also judgment, that is, the giving of a just sentence, which is an act of justice belonging to the judge, whose part it is to give a just decision in every case; [[2:9|and equity|et æquitatem]], that is, justice tempered with clemency out of true discernment, [[2:9|and every good path|et omnem semitam bonam]], that is, virtuous action, which leads rightly to the last end.

paras.t: Si intraverit sapientia cor tuum, ita quod intellectum tuum inhabitet ac informet, et scientia, quæ est donum unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, animæ tuæ placuerit efficaciter per effectum, ita quod non quieveris nisi istam scientiam possederis ; consilium custodiet te : quia sapientia et scientia instruent te ad consulendum tibi ipsi qualiter debeas te habere, et pericula præcavere. Facient quoque te docilem atque benevolum ad obtemperandum sanis aliorum consiliis. Hæc etenim dona Spiritus Sancti instigant hominem, ut nequaquam constituat sibi finem in rebus creatis, caducis, sed in Deo dumtaxat. Hinc et Seneca in suis Proverbiis : Oratorem, inquit, te putes, si tibi ipsi quod oportet persuaseris. Cyrillus quoque in Proverbiorum suorum asserit libro : Prudentia non calliditate, sed consilio vero tuetur prudentem.
paras.en: [[2:10|If wisdom shall enter into thy heart|Si intraverit sapientia cor tuum]], so as to dwell in thy understanding and inform it, [[2:10|and knowledge|et scientia]], which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]] [the margin reads "s. xi, 2", that is, Isaias 11:2], shall effectually, in its effect, [[2:10|please thy soul|animæ tuæ placuerit]], so that thou wilt not rest until thou possess this knowledge: [[2:11|Counsel shall keep thee|consilium custodiet te]]; for wisdom and knowledge will teach thee to take counsel with thyself how thou oughtest to behave and to beware of dangers. They will also make thee teachable and well disposed to follow the sound counsels of others. For these gifts of the Holy Ghost urge a man by no means to set his end in created and perishable things, but in God alone. Hence Seneca too in his *Proverbs*: Think thyself an orator, he says, if thou hast persuaded thyself of what thou oughtest. And Cyril asserts in his book of *Proverbs*: Prudence guards the prudent man not by cunning but by true counsel.

paras.t: Et prudentia servabit te, id est, a periculis præservabit. Ideo subditur, ut eruaris a via mala, id est actione iniqua, quæ ad perditionem deducit, et virtuti contrariatur : quam prudentia facit cognosci ac evitari ; et ab homine qui perversa loquitur, id est a seductoribus et mendosis. Qui derelinquunt iter rectum, id est viam justitiæ, legem divinam, præceptum Dei, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas, id est per habitus vitiosos, per consuetudines pravas, per hæreses et errores.
paras.en: [[2:11|and prudence shall preserve thee|Et prudentia servabit te]], that is, shall preserve thee from dangers. Therefore it is added: [[2:12|That thou mayst be delivered from the evil way|ut eruaris a via mala]], that is, from wicked action, which leads to perdition and is contrary to virtue, and which prudence makes known and avoided; [[2:12|and from the man that speaketh perverse things|et ab homine qui perversa loquitur]], that is, from seducers and liars. [[2:13|Who leave the right way|Qui derelinquunt iter rectum]], that is, the way of justice, the divine law, the precept of God, [[2:13|and walk by dark ways|et ambulant per vias tenebrosas]], that is, by vicious habits, by evil customs, by heresies and errors.

paras.t: Qui lætantur quum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis. Peccant enim ex habitu vitioso. Habitus autem est quasi altera natura, et facit hominem delectari in his ad quæ inclinat. Tales quoque apprehendunt mala ac pessima sub ratione apparenti bonorum ac optimorum. Ideo delectantur in malis ac pessimis, quemadmodum virtuosi in bonis et optimis. Tales etiam sunt adeo excæcati, quod non advertunt sua pericula, peccantque sine remorsu ac freno, imo de vitiis suis se jactant. De quibus dicitur in Isaia : Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt. Hinc demum in epistola Joannis asseritur : Qui odit fratrem suum, in tenebris est, et in tenebris ambulat, et nescit quo eat : quoniam tenebræ excæcaverunt oculos ejus. Denique Ethicorum tertio ait Philosophus : Qualis unusquisque est, talis sibi finis videtur. Ideo vitiosi, in rebus fœdis et voluptuosis, vanis ac pessimis constituunt sibi finem, et delectantur in talibus. Atque, ut rursus docet Aristoteles, Signum habitus est delectatio conjuncta operationi ex habitu procedenti. Qui ergo in peccatis est habituatus, delectatur quum male egerit, et exsultat in pessimis. Propterea Seneca protestatur, gravissimum esse imperium consuetudinis, quia videlicet sic subjicit hominem sibi, ut sibi, non rationi obediat.
paras.en: [[2:14|Who are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in the most wicked things|Qui lætantur quum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis]]. For they sin from a vicious habit; and habit is like a second nature, and makes a man delight in the things to which it inclines him. Such men also take evil and most wicked things under the apparent aspect of good and best things; therefore they delight in evil and most wicked things, as the virtuous delight in good and best things. Such men are also so blinded that they do not notice their own dangers, and they sin without remorse or restraint; nay, they boast of their vices. Of whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 3:9|they have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom, and they have not hid it|Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt]] [the margin reads "id. iii, 9", that is, Isaias 3:9]. Hence too it is asserted in the Epistle of John: [[1 John 2:11|he that hateth his brother is in darkness and walketh in darkness and knoweth not whither he goeth: because the darkness hath blinded his eyes|Qui odit fratrem suum, in tenebris est, et in tenebris ambulat, et nescit quo eat : quoniam tenebræ excæcaverunt oculos ejus]] [the margin gives only "Joann. ii"; the words are 1 John 2:11]. Lastly, in the third book of the *Ethics* the Philosopher says: As each man is, such does the end seem to him. Therefore the vicious set their end in foul and voluptuous, vain and most wicked things, and delight in such. And, as Aristotle teaches again, the sign of a habit is the delight joined to the activity that proceeds from the habit. He, then, who has become habituated to sins delights when he has done evil, and rejoices in the most wicked things. For this reason Seneca declares that the rule of custom is most heavy, because it so subjects a man to itself that he obeys it and not reason.

paras.t: Quorum viæ perversæ sunt : quia actiones eorum sunt saluti contrariæ ; et infames, id est mali, sunt gressus, id est processus conversationis eorum. Nam publice peccant, et alios scandalizant : idcirco a sapientibus contemnuntur ut tales, ac merito diffamantur.
paras.en: [[2:15|Whose ways are perverse|Quorum viæ perversæ sunt]], because their actions are contrary to salvation; and [[2:15|infamous|infames]], that is, evil, are [[2:15|their steps|gressus]], that is, the course of their conduct. For they sin publicly and scandalize others; therefore they are despised as such by the wise, and are deservedly defamed.

paras.t: Ut eruaris a muliere aliena, et ab extranea, id est adultera ac fornicaria, quæ mollit sermones suos, id est, verba blanda, procatoria, libidinosaque profert, ut alliciat ad peccandum, et relinquit ducem pubertatis suæ, id est priorem maritum, quem sumpsit, ductoremque habuit in adolescentia sua, dum annos habuit pubertatis, et pacti Dei sui oblita est, id est legis divinæ ac præcepti quo adulterium et fornicatio prohibentur. Vel etiam violat pactum, quod tempore connubii iniit cum marito, cui fidelitatem promisit : quod et Deus ab initio ordinavit, dicendo per Adam : Relinquet homo patrem suum et matrem, et adhærebit uxori suæ, et erunt duo in carne una. Unde et per Prophetam dicitur : Hæc particeps tua, et uxor fœderis tui. Inclinata est enim ad mortem domus ejus, id est cor in quo per pravitatis suæ consensum moratur, vel caro in qua turpiter delectatur, seu conversatio prava, qua regitur ; vel, Domus, id est domestici ejus, qui ei in peccatis communicant : qui ad mortem culpæ inclinant se, et secundum legem Moysis corporali morti addicebantur ac lapidabantur. Et ad inferos semitæ ipsius, id est, actiones nefariæ appropinquant inferno, et illuc ducunt.
paras.en: [[2:16|That thou mayst be delivered from the strange woman|Ut eruaris a muliere aliena]], [[2:16|and from the stranger|et ab extranea]], that is, the adulteress and harlot, [[2:16|who softeneth her words|quæ mollit sermones suos]], that is, utters soft, wooing and lustful words to entice to sin, [[2:17|And forsaketh the guide of her youth|et relinquit ducem pubertatis suæ]], that is, her first husband, whom she took and had as her guide in her youth, when she was of the age of puberty, [[2:18|And hath forgotten the covenant of her God|et pacti Dei sui oblita est]], that is, the divine law and precept by which adultery and fornication are forbidden[[Ex 20:14||]] [the margin reads "Exod. xv, 14"; the commandment is Exodus 20:14]. Or else she breaks the covenant which she made with her husband at the time of marriage, to whom she promised fidelity: which God also ordained from the beginning, saying through Adam: [[Gen 2:24|a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh|Relinquet homo patrem suum et matrem, et adhærebit uxori suæ, et erunt duo in carne una]]. Whence it is also said through the Prophet: [[Mal 2:14|she was thy partner, and the wife of thy covenant|Hæc particeps tua, et uxor fœderis tui]]. [[2:18|for her house inclineth unto death|Inclinata est enim ad mortem domus ejus]], that is, the heart in which she dwells by consent to her wickedness, or the flesh in which she basely takes her pleasure, or the evil conduct by which she is ruled; or, *house*, that is, her household, who share with her in her sins: who incline themselves to the death of sin, and under the law of Moses were sentenced to bodily death and stoned[[Lev 20:10||]]. [[2:18|and her paths to hell|Et ad inferos semitæ ipsius]], that is, her wicked deeds draw near to hell and lead there.

paras.t: Omnes qui ingrediuntur ad eam, adulterando cum ipsa, non revertentur ad Deum per pœnitentiam veram : quoniam tales vel raro, aut nunquam veraciter pœnitent ; vel tam pauci ex eis convertuntur, quod comparatione non redeuntium, quasi nulli videntur. Nec apprehendent semitas vitæ, id est actus virtutum, seu habitum gratiæ, quæ est vita animæ. Hinc, secundum Philosophum, Qui peccant ex habitu vitioso, sunt incurabiles, quia difficulter valde curantur : quamvis ab omnipotenti animarum medico queant curari, apud quem non est impossibile, imo neque difficile, omne verbum.
paras.en: [[2:19|None that go in unto her|Omnes qui ingrediuntur ad eam]], by committing adultery with her, [[2:19|shall return again|non revertentur]] to God by true penance: because such men either rarely or never truly repent, or so few of them are converted that, compared with those who do not come back, they seem as none. [[2:19|neither shall they take hold of the paths of life|Nec apprehendent semitas vitæ]], that is, the acts of the virtues, or the habit of grace, which is the life of the soul. Hence, according to the Philosopher, those who sin from a vicious habit are incurable, because they are cured only with great difficulty: though they can be cured by the almighty physician of souls, with whom no word is impossible[[Luke 1:37||]], nay, nor even hard[[Jer 32:17||]][[Jer 32:27||]].

paras.t: Quidam per mulierem alienam atque extraneam, ad litteram intelligunt idololatriam, quæ alienat a Deo. Sed expositio ista spiritualis potius esse censetur. Quamvis enim idololatria in Scripturis fornicatio et adulterium aliquando appelletur, non tamen ad litteram solet mulier aliena aut extranea nuncupari ; nec idololatriæ competit relinquere ducem pubertatis suæ, id est Deum, ut ipsi exponunt, quoniam Deus nunquam fuit sponsus aut dux idololatriæ. Spiritualiter vero potest per mulierem hanc congregatio hæreticorum intelligi : quæ mollit verba eloquentiæ suæ, et vana promittit, atque carnalia pollicetur ; ad quam qui introierit, vix redibit, quum dicat Apostolus : Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita, sciens quia subversus est.
paras.en: Some understand by the strange woman and the stranger, according to the letter, idolatry, which estranges from God. But that exposition is rather to be judged a spiritual one. For although idolatry is sometimes called fornication and adultery in the Scriptures[[Osee 1:2||]][[Osee 2:2||]][[Osee 2:5||]][[Osee 3:1||]], it is not usually called, according to the letter, a strange or foreign woman; nor does it fit idolatry to forsake [[2:17|the guide of her youth|ducem pubertatis suæ]], that is, God, as they expound it, since God was never the spouse or guide of idolatry. Spiritually, however, this woman may be understood as the congregation of heretics, which softens the words of its eloquence, promises vain things and offers carnal things; and whoever goes in to it will hardly come back, since the Apostle says: [[Tit 3:10|A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid|Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita]]: [[Tit 3:11|Knowing that he that is such an one is subverted|sciens quia subversus est]].

paras.t: Porro, quod sequitur, ut ambules in via bona, id est, conversatione justa tendas ad gloriam, et calles, id est præcepta, documenta, exempla, justorum custodias, refertur ad illud quod dictum est : Consilium custodiet te, etc.
paras.en: Further, what follows, [[2:20|That thou mayst walk in a good way|ut ambules in via bona]], that is, mayst tend towards glory by just conduct, [[2:20|and mayst keep the paths|et calles]], that is, the precepts, teachings and examples, [[2:20|of the just|justorum custodias]], refers back to what was said: [[2:11|Counsel shall keep thee|Consilium custodiet te]], etc.

paras.t: Qui enim recti sunt corde, videlicet justi, quorum corda sunt linealiter ac directe ad Deum erecta, et vitiorum obliquitatem devitant, habitabunt in terra : quoniam jam per gratiam, fidem et caritatem requiescunt in militanti Ecclesia, quæ peregrinatur in terra ; deinde per gloriam et beatificam fruitionem æternaliter commorabuntur in Ecclesia triumphanti, in terra et regione vivorum ac Beatorum. Nunc quoque in terra sui corporis habitant bene, quia illud habent rationi subjectum, atque in spiritus servitutem redactum : juxta quem sensum ait Salvator, Beati mites, quoniam ipsi hereditabunt terram.
